findings.title: Provider failure in a review step is logged as an "unexpected error" with a full traceback
findings.description: The new `except ProviderError` branch in `_run_part` no longer re-raises. It builds the failed result itself. Before this change the re-raise reached `execute`'s catch-all at line 181, which is the only place that logs "unexpected error". Moving that log call into the branch carries the wording over, but a `ProviderError` is a named, expected failure. The dispatch and summary actions log named provider failures at ERROR with no traceback ("issue 200" convention, `dispatch.py:457`, `summary.py`). Here the same event now produces two lines: a WARNING a few lines up that names the failure artifact, then an ERROR with a traceback saying "unexpected". That is misleading in diagnostics and inconsistent with the sibling actions. Use `_logger.error("review: step %s failed: %s", ...)`, or drop the extra line, since the WARNING already covers the event.

findings.title: Failed-review cost is resolved twice, and the second pass ignores the first result
findings.description: `review_client.py:315` resolves cost for a failed review and stores it on `exc.cost_usd` and `exc.cost_basis`. The failure artifact renders those values through `RunCost.from_error`. `record_from_error` then ignores them and calls `_build`, which runs `resolve_cost` again from `telemetry.cost_usd`. This breaks the "one place the precedence lives" intent. The persisted `UsageRecord` and the failure artifact are computed on separate paths, so they can drift apart. The second pass also emits the alias-pricing warning a second time for the same failure. `record_from_review` already reuses `result.cost_usd` and `result.cost_basis`. `record_from_error` should do the same with `exc.cost_usd` and `exc.cost_basis`.

findings.title: Per-run pricing-warning dedup is bypassed for reviews
findings.description: `run_review_with_profile` calls `resolve_cost(..., set())` with a fresh set on every call, at lines 315 and 321. The executor comment (`executor.py`, "One per run: its pricing-warning set makes each WARNING once per alias") and `test_pricing_warning_once_per_capture` promise one warning per alias per run. A pipeline with several reviews, or split-review parts, on an alias with incomplete pricing now warns once per review instead of once per alias. Standalone `sq review` is unaffected. Accept an optional `warned` set from the caller, and have `ReviewAction` pass the capture's set.

findings.title: `sq stats reviews --json` emits non-JSON text when the review directory is missing
findings.description: The `missing_dir` check runs before the `as_json` branch. With `--json` and no review directory, stdout is the plain string `No review directory at ...` with exit code 0. Any script piping it into `json.loads` will fail. The missing-directory case should produce an empty JSON report (`rows: []`, with the report's `missing_dir` flag in the payload) under `--json`. The plain-text message should be used only for the table output. `reviews_report_json` also does not serialize `missing_dir`, so it should be added. No test covers `--json` with a missing directory.

findings.title: `_row` raises a `ValueError` only to catch it two lines later
findings.description: The `raise ValueError(...)` inside the `try` is caught by the immediately following `except ValueError`. It works, but a plain `isinstance` guard that returns the unreadable row would be clearer and would avoid the raise-to-catch pattern.

findings.title: `UsageCapture(set())` constructor leaks an implementation detail
findings.description: Every caller, including about 25 test sites and the executor, passes a bare `set()`. A default (`warned: set[str] | None = None`, creating an empty set) or an internal-only set would remove the repetition. This also ties into the dedup finding above, because ownership of that set should be explicit.

findings.title: `dispatch.py` keeps growing past the file-size guideline
findings.description: The file is well over the ~300-line guideline, and `_dispatch_session` and `_dispatch_agent` each now carry a near-identical `try/except ProviderError → capture.record_from_telemetry → _provider_failure` block. The `_one_shot` extraction helps. Consider moving the shared failure-to-record step into a helper on `UsageCapture` or `DispatchAction`, which would also keep these functions within the ~50-line target.

findings.title: Usage capture design and test coverage
findings.description: Record building is centralized, cancellation propagates without writing a record, and missing capture fails explicitly through `UsageCaptureMissingError` instead of silently skipping. Unreported values stay `None` rather than becoming 0, and malformed SDK values warn and fall back to `None`. Tests cover the real-fixture reader, the multi-result sum, the stall and drain partial case, the pre-slice state round-trip, and the CLI table and JSON output. I read `review.py` and `dispatch.py` around the changed hunks, and the except-clause ordering in `dispatch.execute` is sound. None of the exceptions that follow `ProviderError` are its subclasses.
